before:
Peat Bothy Custodians — Seasonal Maintenance Manual, Section 4

Each bothy is visited twice yearly by the district custodian, who carries out such repairs as the stores allow. Where the visit's time or materials fall short, the custodian works down the settled order: roof coverings are attended to before window glazing, and window glazing before floor boarding. Nothing here widens or narrows what a custodian may undertake; the same repairs remain open in every case, and any of them may be deferred to the following visit if the weather forbids. Custodians should note the deferred items on the back of the visit slip so that the next caller arrives with the right materials in the pannier.
after:
Peat Bothy Custodians — Seasonal Maintenance Manual, Section 4

Nothing here widens or narrows what a custodian may undertake; the same repairs remain open in every case, and any of them may be deferred to the following visit if the weather forbids. variation_site: Section 4 sets out how a short visit is worked through.
author_note: Reverses the settled working order while every permitted repair stays available.

before:
County Herbarium — Accession Catalogue, Preliminary Notes

This part of the catalogue lists sheets received from private collections since the last binding. Depositors are reminded that sheets arriving without a collecting locality cannot be given a full entry and will be held in the pending drawer until the gap is filled. Each entry gives the family, the collector's initials, the date of gathering where known, and the drawer in which the sheet now sits. Sheets lent out to other institutions carry a slip in place of the specimen. Queries about any entry should be put to the herbarium clerk on Thursday mornings, when the drawers are open for consultation.
after:

before:
Tidal Crossing Ferry Service — Notice to Users, Slipway Board

The smaller of the two craft working the crossing, the Kestrel, is entered on the service list as a passenger launch. Sailings are as printed on the tide card, with the last crossing an hour before low water. Users are reminded that the slipway is slippery on the ebb and that the handrail was renewed in March. Bicycles travel free; dogs travel on a lead. Any change to the printed sailing times will be chalked on this board by the boatman on the morning of the change, and also telephoned through to the post office at Aiden Ferry.

before:
Chalk Downs Water Bailiffs — Field Handbook, Section 12: Springs

The head spring above Cranwell Bottom is believed to run dry in most Augusts, and bailiffs walking the upper beat should carry water rather than rely on it. The lower flushes hold longer, though they too fall away in a dry year. Where the spring is found flowing in late summer, note the date on the beat card; where it is found dry, note that as well, since the beat cards are the only continuous account kept of the upper water. Bailiffs new to the beat should walk it once with an experienced hand before taking it alone.

before:
Marsh Drainage Board — Sluice Keeper's Daily Log, Week 33

Tuesday: wind fresh from the north-east, no rain overnight. The upstream gauge read 1.42 metres at 0600 and was falling slowly through the morning. Both leaves of the middle sluice were raised two notches at 0730 and dropped again at 1100. The weed screen was cleared twice; the second clearing brought up a quantity of cut reed from the upper cut, which suggests the contractors are working above the bend. Grease was put to the winding gear on the east leaf. Nothing else to report. Keeper off duty from 1600, relief keeper telephoned and acknowledged the handover.

before:
Moorland Rescue Post — Duty Cover Policy, Appendix

The post keeps one warden on call at all times, drawn from the two standing rotas. The main body of this document sets out what the on-call warden must carry, when the post may be left unattended, and how cover is handed over at the change of shift. This appendix records only the working arrangement for the coming quarter: the Tuesday night slot falls to the warden on B rota, with the remaining nights shared as before. Wardens who cannot take an allotted night arrange a swap between themselves and tell the post secretary, who keeps the wall chart up to date.

before:
Silver Band Instrument Store — Annual Report to the Committee

The store was checked over the last weekend in October by the librarian and two players. Instruments coming back from loan are weighed, then tagged, then photographed, and the sheet is passed to the treasurer for the insurance schedule. Nothing in this year's checking altered what the band owns or what players owe on a loaned instrument; two euphonium cases are past mending and a replacement mouthpiece was bought for the second cornet. The committee is asked to note the report and to consider whether the store's dehumidifier, now nine years old, should be replaced before next winter.

before:
Branch Library Interlending — Counter Settings Sheet

This sheet governs what the counter terminal does when a borrowed volume comes back late. Charges are worked out using the sliding daily scale, applied from the day after the due date and capped at the replacement cost of the volume. Concessionary borrowers are handled by the same setting with the pensioner flag on. Reservations, renewals and lost-item billing are untouched by this sheet and are set elsewhere. Staff changing anything here should initial the amendment column and tell the branch supervisor, since the county returns are drawn straight from the terminal at the end of each quarter.
after:
Branch Library Interlending — Counter Settings Sheet

variation_site: The sheet covers what happens when a volume comes back late.
author_note: Swaps which charging scheme the terminal applies to derive the figure.

before:

Inspectors complete one line per apiary and post the sheet to the district office at the end of the week. Dates of visit are entered as 04/09/2026, the columns for hive counts take whole numbers only, and the notes column is left blank unless something needs saying. The office keys the sheets into the county system on Monday, so a sheet arriving after Monday's post waits a week. Inspectors should keep the carbon copy in the visit book. Sheets with a column left empty are returned to the inspector rather than guessed at by the office.

before:
Canal Basin Moorings — Registry Preface

For the purposes of every table that follows, a working craft is one moved under its own power at least twice in a calendar year. The counts in Table 1, the berth allocations in Table 2 and the reduced dues listed in Table 3 all follow from that definition, and a craft's standing is reviewed each January against the lock-keeper's passage book. Owners who dispute their entry may ask for the passage book to be consulted at the basin office. Craft laid up for repair keep their standing for one further year, after which they are entered among the static craft.
after:
Canal Basin Moorings — Registry Preface

For the purposes of every table that follows, a working craft is one moved under its own power at least six times in a calendar year. The counts in Table 1, the berth allocations in Table 2 and the reduced dues listed in Table 3 all follow from that definition, and a craft's standing is reviewed each January against the lock-keeper's passage book. Owners who dispute their entry may ask for the passage book to be consulted at the basin office. Craft laid up for repair keep their standing for one further year, after which they are entered among the static craft.
variation_site: The preface fixes the working craft definition used throughout.
author_note: Moves the founding definition that the tables downstream all compose over.

before:
Upland Seed Bank — Management Committee, Minutes of the March Meeting

Present: four members and the curator; apologies from the treasurer. The curator reported that the bank holds 412 accessions, of which a little over a third are grasses gathered from the eastern hills. Germination testing has fallen behind by about two seasons owing to the loss of the second incubator. The committee agreed to seek a quotation for a replacement and to write to the moorland trust about access to the Fell Head site in July. Date of the next meeting: the second Thursday in June, at the field centre as usual.
